acceptance_criteria: Unexpected storage verification errors return the stable STORAGE_PROVIDER_UNAVAILABLE 503 envelope without provider internals.
The upload attempt is released so the same finalize request can be retried after the provider recovers.
Backend regression tests, typecheck/build, progress and handoff evidence are updated.
features.evidence: Completed on 2026-09-28. Finalization now releases the attempt and returns a sanitized 503 STORAGE_PROVIDER_UNAVAILABLE envelope for unexpected storage SDK/provider errors instead of leaking an opaque 500; callers can retry the same attempt after recovery. Regression coverage exercises both explicit and unexpected provider failures and verifies provider details are absent. Verification: recorder routes 21/21; full backend 90 passed/5 opt-in skipped plus typecheck/build; no production token or object was replayed.

features.name: Recover stale finalization on asset removal
features.description: Allow failed uploads whose finalization worker died to be removed while preserving protection for a currently running finalization.
acceptance_criteria: DELETE keeps rejecting a recently active finalization to avoid races.
DELETE atomically expires a finalizing attempt older than two minutes and discards its asset with normal provider cleanup.
Repository integration coverage, API documentation, typecheck/build, progress and handoff evidence are updated.
features.evidence: Completed on 2026-09-28. Asset discard still protects a recently updated finalizing attempt, but atomically expires a finalizing attempt older than two minutes before soft-discard, recovering assets stranded by a crashed worker. Verification: backend full suite 90 passed/5 opt-in skipped plus typecheck/build; PostgreSQL repository integration 2/2 including stale-finalization recovery; API contract, progress and handoff updated.

features.name: Session-scoped storage status and settings provider management
features.description: Avoid repeated storage provider probes during a signed-in session and move Google Drive connection controls into Settings.
acceptance_criteria: Storage provider availability is fetched once per authenticated browser session and reused across page navigation and focus changes.
The existing inline Refresh storage action force-refreshes the cached provider status and preserves selected files.
Google Drive connection/reconnect/unlink controls are shown in Settings rather than the profile popup, with UI tests and build evidence updated.
features.evidence: Completed on 2026-09-28. Storage provider availability is cached in the browser API module for the authenticated session, while the existing storage-providers-changed event and inline Refresh storage action force an explicit refresh; focus and page navigation no longer probe the endpoint repeatedly. Google Drive connection/reconnect/unlink controls were removed from the profile popup and added to Settings. Verification: web 51/51 plus typecheck/build; provider cache and Settings/profile regressions pass.

features.name: Load primary pages on first visit
features.description: Defer Workspace, Archive and Settings mounting and data requests until each page is opened, retaining visited page state within the signed-in session.
acceptance_criteria: Initial and direct page loads do not mount or fetch data for unvisited primary pages.
Visited pages retain drafts and settings state during navigation without rerunning mount requests.
Signing out clears retained pages; navigation regressions, web checks and session evidence are updated.
features.evidence: Completed on 2026-09-29. Primary pages mount only on first visit, then retain their state during authenticated navigation; logout/user changes reset retained pages and visit history. Header logout now uses the shared storage-cache reset handler. Verification: ./init.sh passed; focused App navigation tests 9/9; full web tests 55/55; web typecheck/build and git diff --check passed. Covers deferred Settings/Drive mounting, direct Archive/Settings entry, preserved drafts/filters/settings, and logout followed by fresh login. No backend/API/migration change or deployment.

Owner-authorized endpoints return a validated Google webViewLink or redirect to it; unavailable, non-ready and foreign assets fail closed.
Clipboard fallback, VI/EN copy, API/storage/UI regressions, checks and documentation are complete; existing verified downloads and Drive permissions remain unchanged.

features.name: Optimistic session restore during backend wake
features.description: Render the signed-in app shell immediately from a remembered user while the silent session check runs in the background, so a cold-starting backend no longer blocks the whole UI behind the full-page skeleton.
acceptance_criteria: With a remembered user in sessionStorage, the workspace/archive/settings shell renders immediately with an accessible 'Restoring session...' status while /auth/session is pending.
A resolved session for the same user keeps mounted page state; a failed or mismatched session downgrades to the signed-out UI and clears the remembered user.
Without a remembered user the previous full-page skeleton behavior is preserved, and expected 401s during the checking phase are not surfaced as storage/settings/history errors.
A best-effort /health request is fired on app load to wake sleeping instances, and web tests, typecheck and build pass.
features.evidence: Completed on 2026-10-03. Added web/src/sessionUserStore.ts (+4 unit tests), pingHealth() in web/src/api.ts, sessionStatus state model with manual-auth race guard in App.tsx, sessionChecking error suppression in RecorderWorkflow/RecorderHistory/GoogleDriveConnection/SettingsPage, and the header 'Restoring session...' status pill (VI/EN). Verification: web 71/71 tests, typecheck, build; backend 93 passed/5 opt-in skipped plus typecheck (unchanged). Headless Chrome against local dev servers: remembered user + held /auth/session showed shell + pill within 1.2s and pill cleared after verification; slow 401 downgraded to login and cleared the store; no remembered user kept the classic skeleton. Follow-up fix: AccountAccess resolved the #header-profile portal target during the render phase, so the first optimistic paint showed the inline 'Signed in as' fallback card in the header while checking; the target is now resolved in useLayoutEffect after commit (headless Chrome: card gone, avatar portals with the restoring pill; web 71/71, typecheck, build). Production cold measurement after 22.5min Render idle: wake request completed in 13.5s via the Vercel proxy (well under the 120s CDN origin timeout), so the transient-failure downgrade path is not expected to trigger. Not deployed to production.

features.name: Compact collapsible archive filters
features.description: The archive filter block occupies most of the first screen and pushes the record list below the fold. Collapse advanced filters (operation, status, order, date range) behind a toggle with an active-count badge, keep search always visible, and auto-apply filter changes so the list is reachable in one glance.
acceptance_criteria: By default only the search row and a filters toggle are visible; the record list starts near the top of the card on mobile and desktop.
Advanced filters live in a collapsible panel with an active-filter count badge; clearing returns to the unfiltered list.
Changing any filter applies immediately (page resets to 1) without a separate Apply step; search still applies on submit and keeps the clear-search control.
Existing filter semantics (reference search, operation, status, order, date range, pagination) are unchanged and VI/EN labels are complete.
Web tests, typecheck and build pass.
features.evidence: Completed on 2026-10-04. features.name: Multi-select delete from the archive list
features.description: Add selection checkboxes to archive list rows with a bulk action bar so owners can delete several completed/expired records at once instead of opening each detail popup. Deletion reuses the existing per-activity delete API and a single confirmation dialog.
acceptance_criteria: Each deletable list row has an accessible checkbox plus a select-all control for the current page; selection survives re-render and resets on page/filter change.
A bulk bar shows the selected count with Delete and Cancel actions; delete requires one confirmation dialog stating evidence is permanently removed.
Non-deletable statuses (draft/uploading/cancelled) cannot be selected for delete and are reported as skipped in the result notice.
Partial failures are reported per record; the list refreshes and shows a VI/EN result summary after the batch.
Web tests, typecheck and build pass.
features.evidence: Completed on 2026-10-04. Pointer-down outside the dialog (and Escape) still closes it; scrolling inside the dialog never moves or hides the header.

features.name: Allow deleting activities in any status
features.description: Owners could not remove cancelled, draft or uploading records at all: the backend delete gate rejected every non-complete status and the archive UI hid the delete control for them. Any activity can now be deleted (single or bulk) through the same soft-delete plus provider cleanup pipeline used by completed records.
acceptance_criteria: DELETE /activities/{id} returns 202 for every status (draft, uploading, complete, expired, cancelled) and enqueues provider cleanup for assets with provider refs; repeat delete stays idempotent.
The detail popup shows Delete for every status and the list checkboxes/select-all include every row.
ACTIVITY_NOT_DELETABLE is removed from service errors and the API contract.
Web and backend tests, typecheck and build pass.
features.evidence: Completed on 2026-10-04. Backend deleteActivity no longer gates on status (only null/already-deleted handled); ACTIVITY_NOT_DELETABLE mapping removed from service.ts and docs/API_CONTRACT.md; every list row and detail popup now exposes delete. features.name: Apply retention setting to existing completed records
features.description: Evidence expiry is frozen at completion time, so raising the auto-delete period (e.g. 1 → 15 days) still deleted records completed under the shorter setting. PATCH /settings must recompute evidence_expires_at (completed_at + current retention) for the owner's still-complete activities in the same transaction.
acceptance_criteria: updateRetentionDays recomputes evidence_expires_at = completed_at + new retention days for all owner activities in status complete; expired/cancelled/deleted rows are untouched.
Setting update and expiry recomputation commit atomically; unknown user returns null as before.
API contract and Settings page copy state that saving updates existing completed records.
Backend and web tests (incl. PostgreSQL integration), typecheck and build pass.
features.evidence: Completed on 2026-10-04. PostgresSettingsRepository.updateRetentionDays now runs in one transaction: after updating app_users.retention_days it recomputes evidence_expires_at = completed_at + new days for the owner's status='complete' activities; expired/cancelled/deleted rows untouched; missing user still returns null. API contract and Settings page copy (EN/VI) state the recalculation. Backend 93 passed/6 opt-in skipped plus typecheck; new PostgreSQL integration 1/1 (recompute to 15 days, expired row unchanged, unknown user null); web 77/77, typecheck, build. Live local API smoke reproducing the reported bug: seeded retention 1 day + a complete record expiring tomorrow, PATCH settings to 15 → 200 and the record's window became exactly 15 days from completion; tightening to 5 recomputed to 5 days; retentionDays=0 → 400. Probe rows, session, token removed and local account retention restored to 30.

ARCHITECTURE.md and OPERATIONS.md describe the daily sweep and owner-configured retention.
Backend tests and typecheck pass.

features.name: Apply audited design-system refinements to the recorder UI
features.description: Seven verified plans under design-plans/ closed gaps that survived feature growth: an element-level 44px minimum that silently overrode every smaller control, record status presented two different ways inside one task, hand-written link styling beside the button primitive, English application copy in the activity detail and shell chrome, CSS re-capitalization of translated labels plus browser-locale dates and byte sizes, an over-provisioned new-record column split, and a step indicator that could not express state.
acceptance_criteria: Control heights are declared by the primitives: standard buttons and fields render 44px, sm renders 36px, icon renders a 40x40 square, the language flag trigger renders its documented compact size, and no !min-h-*/!important height patch remains in web/src.
Record status uses Badge plus statusVariant in both the archive row and the detail header, and evidence/Drive action links render through buttonVariants.
Activity detail copy, archive pagination, new-record section names and shell navigation/footer labels resolve through t() in both locales.
Translated labels are not re-cased by CSS, and dates plus byte sizes format through useI18n().locale.
The new-record card splits its lg columns equally with the drop zone filling the row, and the step indicator advances with items.length, activityId and complete.
Web tests, typecheck and the production build pass.

Detail header renders the outline status Badge for a draft (measured 77x26) and its meta line reads 'Bản nháp · 22:14 4 thg 10, 2026 · Bộ nhớ ứng dụng'; the list row reads 'Đóng gói' instead of 'Đóng Gói'.
